rows.question: My tenant isn't paying rent, what can I do?
queries: My tenant isn't paying rent, what can I do?
tenant default in payment of rent forfeiture determination of lease
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 section 111 determination of lease forfeiture
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 section 114 relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent
topSources: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s111
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s114
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s112
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s114A
rows.answer:
Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for non-payment of rent and the lessor sues to eject the lessee, the lessee may pay or tender the rent in arrear with interest and full costs, or give security, at the hearing of the suit, under Section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [2].

Conditions and time limits:
- If the tenant gives security for making the payment, it must be done within fifteen days, as provided under Section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [2].
- For a tenant under the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, if a Revenue-officer causes a notice to be served regarding a decree for arrears of rent, the tenant must pay the amount within fifteen days from receipt of the notice to avoid ejectment under Section 44 of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 [4].

- For offences punishable with imprisonment of less than three years, no arrest of a person who is infirm or above sixty years of age shall be made without the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police [1].

rows.question: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?
queries: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?
suit for recovery of money lent limitation period
Limitation Act 1963 article 19 suit for money payable for money lent
Limitation Act 1963 section 18 effect of acknowledgment in writing
rows.answer:
The period of limitation for filing a suit for money payable for money lent is three years from when the loan is made, as provided under Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [3]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- Period of limitation: Three years [3].
- Time from which the period begins to run: When the loan is made [3].
- For money lent under an agreement that it shall be payable on demand, the period of limitation is also three years beginning from when the loan is made, as provided under Article 21 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [4].

- A condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court [1].

rows.question: My husband beats me. What law protects me?
queries: My husband beats me. What law protects me?

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 section 12 application to Magistrate

topSources: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 s12
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 s5
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 s2
rows.answer:
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides a civil law remedy for the protection of women from domestic violence, and Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860) makes cruelty by a husband or his relative an offence [2][10][11].

- Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 allows an aggrieved person, a Protection Officer, or any other person on her behalf to present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs [1].
- Section 23 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 empowers the Magistrate to pass interim and ex parte orders in proceedings under the Act [6].
- Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes a husband or relative of the husband who subjects a woman to cruelty with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also makes them liable to fine [2].

rows.question: What is the punishment for drunk driving?
queries: What is the punishment for drunk driving?
driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs punishment
Motor Vehicles Act section 185 driving under influence of alcohol or drugs
Motor Vehicles Act section 202 power to arrest without warrant for drunken driving
topSources: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, 4 of 1939 (Rep., Act 59 of 1988) s117
rows.answer:
Whoever, while driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle, has in his blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. detected in a breath analyser test, or is under the influence of a drug making him incapable of exercising proper control, shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term up to six months, with a fine up to two thousand rupees, or with both, under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1][5]. For a second or subsequent offence committed within three years of the previous similar offence, the punishment is imprisonment up to two years, a fine up to three thousand rupees, or both, under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1][5].

Related provisions:
- Section 202 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 covers the power of a police officer in uniform to arrest without warrant for an offence punishable under section 185, subject to medical examination conditions [2].
- Section 203 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 covers breath tests by police or authorized motor vehicles department officers where there is reasonable cause to suspect an offence under section 185 [8].

rows.question: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?
queries: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?

rows.answer:
No petition for divorce can be presented to any court unless one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage, as provided in Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 [1], and Section 29 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 [2]. Similarly, under Section 32B of the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936, no suit for divorce by mutual consent shall be filed unless one year has lapsed since the date of the marriage [8].

Conditions and time limits:
- A court may allow a petition to be presented before one year has elapsed upon an application made in accordance with High Court rules, on the ground of exceptional hardship to the petitioner or exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent, under Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 [1].
- A district court may similarly allow a petition to be presented before one year has passed on the ground of exceptional hardship suffered by the petitioner or exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent, under Section 29 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 [2].

queries: cheque bounce ho gaya kya karu

The Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 section 138
The Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 section 142 cognizance of offences
rows.answer:
A person commits an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, when a cheque drawn on their bank account for the discharge of a legally enforceable debt or other liability is returned unpaid by the bank due to insufficient funds or because it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid by agreement [1].

Conditions and time limits:
- The cheque must be presented to the bank within six months from the date it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier [1].
- The payee or holder in due course must make a demand for payment by giving a written notice to the drawer within thirty days of receiving information from the bank about the return of the cheque [1].
- The drawer of the cheque has fifteen days from the receipt of the notice to make the payment [1].

Related provisions:
- Section 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, covers cognizance of offences, requiring a written complaint by the payee or holder in due course within one month of the cause of action arising, to be tried by a court not inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class [2].

As observed in the Supreme Court judgment Gurcharan Singh & Ors. versus State (Delhi Administration), if there appear to be reasonable grounds to believe the accused is guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, a ban is imposed against granting bail, but in all other non-bailable cases judicial discretion will be exercised in favour of granting bail subject to conditions [12].
